title: Pitches from women that include the borrower's specific age are associated with increased funding speed.
Female borrowers who mention previous loans or promise prompt repayment may fund more slowly.
Male borrowers who provide specific details about current hardships fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who explicitly describe themselves as a mother may fund more slowly.
Pitches from women that are significantly shorter than their counterparts tend to experience increased funding speed.
Female borrowers who mention the number of children and their schooling may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who express explicit gratitude to lenders or institutions may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who mention existing debts or arrears may fund more slowly.
Pitches from women that explicitly reference a history of successful loan repayments or previous financial history accelerate funding speed.
Female borrowers who mention being married may fund more slowly.
Female borrowers who list specific products or goals beyond family welfare fund faster.
Female borrowers who mention benefits to their family or community fund faster.
Specifying the number of years a business has operated predicts faster funding regardless of gender.
Pitches that provide concrete financial figures or specific inventory lists fund faster regardless of gender.
Mentioning family obligations and benefits has opposite effects on funding speed by gender.
Mentioning local currency amounts or specific institutional affiliations predicts slower funding regardless of gender.
Female borrowers who list the specific ages of their children fund faster.
Female borrowers who use generic template language fund more slowly.
